URL: https://understandingwar.org/research/russia-ukraine/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-july-18-2026/
Retrieved via Exa web_fetch 19 July 2026. ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, July 18, 2026. Author: Jordan Glynn.

KEY TAKEAWAYS:
1. Russian Chief of General Staff Gen Valery Gerasimov again aggrandised Russian battlefield advances in Donetsk Oblast on July 18 in a choreographed HQ inspection; several claims (entering Dobropillya, Hannivka, Oleksiyevo-Druzhkivka, Svitle, Krasnoyarske) not corroborated by any evidence. ISW assesses Russia LOST terrain at ~1.6 sq km/day July 1-17.
2. Continued Ukrainian strikes on vessels in Black Sea and Sea of Azov are compelling Russia to divert elite drone units (up to 200 Rubikon crews) from the frontline. USF commander Brovdi: Ukraine struck 172 Russian naval vessels in past 13 days.
3. Ukrainian forces struck two logistics facilities of Wildberries (Russia's largest online retailer, "Russia's Amazon") overnight July 17-18 in Elektrostal (Moscow Oblast) and Kotovsk (Tambov Oblast), causing fires. Estimated losses up to ~100 billion roubles (~$1.28bn); ~10-15% of Wildberries warehouse space damaged. Moscow Oblast governor: Elektrostal strike injured 37, killed 1; Tambov governor: Kotovsk strike injured 25, killed 7.
4. Mykolaiv Oblast Military Administration Head Vitaly Kim resigned July 17 (to become minister of veterans' affairs).
5. Ukrainian forces struck Russian oil/energy infrastructure overnight July 17-18 (Nefto-Service oil depot, Noginsk, Moscow Oblast; Kursk power facility, 46,000+ consumers lost power).
6. Neither side made confirmed advances July 18.
7. Russia launched two Iskander-M ballistic missiles, two Onyx anti-ship missiles, three Kh-59/69 cruise missiles and 90 drones against Ukraine overnight; main direction Odesa Oblast. Double-tap strike on a house in Derhachi, Kharkiv Oblast.
8. Ukrainian 425th Skala Regiment posted footage holding a flag in western Kostyantynivka, claiming control; ISW cannot confirm full control.
